Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ১) A student scores 55% marks in 8 papers of 100 marks each. He scores 15% of his total marks in English. How much does he score in English?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Total marks obtained by the student = 55% of 800
= {(55/100) × 800}
= 440
 ∴ Marks scored in English
= 15% of 440
= {(15/100) × 440}
= 66

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ২) A number increased by 37.5% gives 33. The number is -
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Let,
the number be x.
Then, (100 + 37.5)% of x
⇒ 137.5% of x = 33
⇒ 137.5 × (1/100) × x = 33
⇒ x = (33 × 100)/137.5
⇒ x = 24.

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ৩) If 75% of a number is added to 75, then the result is the number itself. The number is -
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Let,
the number be x.
Then, 75% of x + 75 = x
⇒ x - 75x/100 = 75
⇒ x - 3x/4 = 75
⇒ x/4 = 75
⇒ x = 300

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ৪) Two tailors X and Y are paid a total of Tk. 550 per week by their employer. If X is paid 20 percent more than the sum paid to Y, how much is Y paid per week?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Let,
the sum paid to Y per week be Tk. x
Then, sum paid to X per week
= 120% of Tk. x
= Tk. (120/100) × x
= Tk. (6/5) x.
∴ x + (6x/5) = 550
⇒ 11x/5 = 550
⇒ x = (550 × 5)/11
= Tk. 250.

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ৫) If 20% of A = 50% of B, what percentage of A is B?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
20% of A = 50% of B
⇒ (20/100) × A = (50/100) × B
⇒ A/5 = B/2
B = 2A/5.
Required percentage = (B/A) × 100%
= (2A/5 × 1/A) × 100%
= {(2×100)/5}%
= 40%

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ৬) The salaries of A and B together amount to Tk. 2000. A spends 95% of his salary and B 85% of his. If now, their savings are the same, what is A’s salary?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Let,
A's salary = Tk. x.
Then, B's salary = Tk. (2000 - x)
According to the question,
(100 - 95)% of A = (100 - 85)% of B
⇒ (5x/100) = (15/100) × (2000 - x)
⇒ x = 1500.

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ৭) A scored 30% marks and failed by 15 marks. B scored 40% marks and obtained 35 marks more than those required to pass. The pass percentage is -
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Let,
total marks = x.
Then,
(30% of x) + 15 = (40% of x) - 35
⇒ (30x/100) + 15 = (40x/100) - 35
⇒ (x/10) = 50
⇒ x = 500.
So, passing marks = (30% of 500) + 15
= (30/100) × 500 + 15
= 165
∴ Pass percentage = {(165/500) × 100}% = 33%.

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ৮) The population of a town 2 years ago was 62,500. Due to migration to big cities, it decreases every year at the rate of 4%. The present population of the town is -
৯) If A’s income is 10% more than B’s, how much percentage is b’s income less than A’s?
১০) In a mixture of milk and water, the proportion of water by weight was 75%. If in the 60 gm mixture 15 gm of water was added, what would be the percentage of water?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Weight of water in 60 gm mixture = 75% of 60 gm
= {(75/100) × 60} gm
= 45 gm.
Weight of water in 75 gms mixture = (45 + 15) gm
= 60 gm.
∴ Required percentage = {(60/75) × 100}%
= 80%.

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ১১) A bicycle originally cost Tk. 100 and was discounted 10%. After three months it was sold after being discounted another 15%. How much was the bicycle sold for?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
According to the question,
Original price = Tk. 100
10% discounted price = Tk. 90
The bicycle was sold after another 15% discount.
Meaning, the bicycle was sold at 85% of the discounted price.
Selling price= Tk. 90 × 85%
= Tk. 76.50

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ১২) A man made a loss of 20% on his cost by selling a pen at taka 200. What should be his selling price in taka if he wants to make a profit of 10% on cost
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
According to the question,
At 20% loss, 80 Tk selling price হলে cost = 100 Tk.
∴ 200 Tk. selling price হলে cost = (100 × 200)/80
= 250 Tk.

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ১৩) Mr. Kamal bought 20 mangoes for Tk. 55. He found that 10% of the mangoes were damaged and sold the rest at the rate of Taka 54 per dozen. How much profit in Taka did he make?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
According to the question,
10% of 20 = 2 mangoes were damaged
∴ বিক্রি করলো 20 - 2
=18
= 1(1/2) dozen.
বিক্রয় মূল্য = 54 × 1(1/2)
= 81
∴ Profit = 81 - 55
= 26.

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ১৪) A pen was sold at 10% loss. If the selling price was Tk. 6 more, then the seller could have made a profit of 5%. What was the purchase price of the pen?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
মনে করি,
ক্রয়মূল্য = 100 টাকা
∴ 10% loss এ বিক্রয়মূল্য = 90 টাকা
এবং 5% profit এ বিক্রয়মূল্য = 105 টাকা
∴ বিক্রয়মূল্য (105 - 90) = 15 টাকা বেশি হলে,
5% profit হতো।
এখন ঐকিক নিয়ম ব্যবহার করে, বিক্রয়মূল্য 15 টাকা বেশি হলে ক্রয়মূল্য 100 টাকা
∴ বিক্রয়মূল্য 1 টাকা বেশি হলে ক্রয়মূল্য (100/15) টাকা
∴ বিক্রয়মূল্য 6 টাকা বেশি ক্রয়মূল্য (100/15) × 6
= 40 টাকা।

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ১৫) The retail price of a pen is 40 taka. Asif got a discount of 20% over the retail price and he eventually saved taka 240 on his total purchase of the pens. How many pens did he buy?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
According to the question,
Retail price 40 Tk. (per pen).
20% discount = 40 × (20/100)
= 8 Tk.
অর্থ্যাৎ,
প্রতি pen এ save হয় = 8 Tk.
Total savings = 240 Tk.
∴ Number of pen = 240/8
= 30 pen.

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ১৬) If you buy equal amounts of two types of chocolate at the rate of Tk. 1/4 and Tk. 1/6 respectively and sell all of them at the rate of Tk. 1/5, what will be your profit/loss?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
মনে করি,
প্রত্যেক ধরনের চকলেট কেনার হলো 60 টি করে।
তাহলে,
Total cost = 60 × (1/4) + 60 × (1/6)
= 25।
আবার, selling price = 60 × 2 × (1/5)
= 24।
কাজেই percentage loss = (25 - 24)/25 × 100
= 4%

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ১৭) A merchant buys two articles for Taka 1400. He sells one of them at a profit of 20% and the others at a loss of 8%. He makes no profit or loss in the end. What is the selling price of the article that he sold at a loss?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
মনে করি,
loss এ sell করা article এর cost price x
profit এ sell করা article এর cost (1400 - x)
এখন, overall কোন profit বা loss নেই,
অর্থ্যাৎ,
দুই article এর profit এবং loss equal.
8x/100 = 20/100(1400 - x)
⇒ 8x = 28000 - 20x
⇒ 28x = 28000
⇒ x = 28000/28
⇒ x = 1000.
অর্থ্যাৎ, Selling price of the article sold at 8% loss = 920 Tk.

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ১৮) A TV and a computer have the same price. If the price of the TV goes up by 20% and that of the computer goes down by 10%, how much more will it cost to buy 4 TV’s and 4 computers?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
ধরি, price x টাকা
TV এর price বাড়ার পর = x + x এর 20%
= 1.2x
Computer এর price কমার পর = x - x এর 10%
= 0.9x
পূর্বে 4 টি TV এবং 4 টি computer এর price = 8x
এখন 4 টি TV এবং 4 টি computer এর price = 4.8x + 3.6x
= 8.4x
দাম বেশি হয় = (8.4x - 8x) = 0.4x টাকা

সুতরাং, খরচ বাড়বে = (0.4/8) × 100
= 5%

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ১৯) Safin has x eggs. He sells 12 of them at a profit of 10 percent and the rest of the eggs at a loss of 10 percent. He made neither profit nor a loss overall. Which one of the following equals x?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Let a Tk be the cost price of each egg to Shafin.
Hence, the net cost of the x eggs is ax Tk.
Now, the selling price of the eggs when selling at a 10% profit is a{1 + (10/100)}
= 11a/10.
Selling 12 eggs now returns 12(11a/10)Tk.
The selling price of the eggs when selling at a 10% loss is a{1 - (10/100)}
= 9a/10.
Selling the remaining (x - 12) eggs now returns (x - 12)(9a/10)
= a(.9x + 2.4)
Since overall he made neither a profit nor a loss, the returns equals the net cost.
So we have a(.9 + 2.4)
= ax.
Dividing both sides by a yields .9x + 2.4 = x.
Multiplying each side by 10 yields 9x + 24 = 10x.
Subtracting 9x from both sides yields x = 24.

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ২০) A trader owes a merchant 10,028 Tk due 1 year hence. The trader wants to settle the account after 3 months. If the rate of interest is 12% per annum, how much cash should he pay
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Required money = Present Worth of Tk. 10028 due 9 months hence
= Tk. [{10028 × 100}/{100 +(12 × 9/12)}]
= Tk. 9200

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ২১) A man purchased a cow for Tk. 3000 and sold it the same day for Tk. 3600, allowing the buyer a credit of 2 years. If the rate of interest be 10% per annum, then the man has a gain of
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Cost price = Tk 3000
Selling price = [{3600 × 100}/{100 + (10 × 2)}]
= Tk. 3000
Gain = 0%.

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ২২) Tk 20 is the true discount on Tk 260 due after a certain time. What will be the true discount on the same sum due after half of the former time, the rate of interest being the same?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Simple Interest on Tk. (260 - 20) for a given time = Tk. 20
Simple Interest on Tk. 240 for half the time = Tk. 10
True Discount On Tk. 250 = Tk. 10.
∴ True Discount On Tk. 260 = Tk. {(10/250) × 260}
= Tk. 10.40

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ২৩) The banker’s discount on a sum of money for 1(1/2) years is Tk. 558 and the true discount on the same sum for 2 years is Tk 600. The rate percent is -
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Banker's Discount for 3/2 years = Tk. 558
Banker's Discount for 2 years = Tk. {558 × (2/3) × 2}
= Tk. 744
True Discount for 2 years = Tk. 600
∴ Sum = {(B.D × T.D)/(B.D - T.D)}
= Tk. {(744 × 600)/(744 - 600)
= Tk. (744 × 600)/144
= TK. 3100
Thus, Tk. 744 is Simple Interest on Tk. 3100 for 2 years
∴ Rate = {(100 × 744)/(3100 × 2)}%
= 12%

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ২৪) The banker’s discount on a certain sum due 2 years hence is 11/10 of the true discount. The rate percent is
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Let
True Discount be Tk.1
Then, Banker's Discount = Tk. 11/10 = Tk. 1.10
∴ Sum = Tk {(1.10 × 1)/(1.10 - 1)}
= Tk (110/10)
= Tk. 11
Simple interest on Tk. 11 for 2 years is Tk 1.10
∴ Rate = {(100 × 1.10)/(11 × 2)%
= 5%

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ২৫) At a club, 70% of the members are women and 60% of the members are married. If ⅔ of the men are single, what fraction of the women are married?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
ধরি,
মোট member = 100
∴ মহিলা member = 70 এবং পুরুষ member = 30 জন।
30 জন পুরুষের মধ্যে অবিবাহিত = 30 × 2/3 = 20 জন।
সুতরাং বিবাহিত = 10 জন।
মোট বিবাহিত = 60 জন।
∴ মহিলাদের মধ্যে বিবাহিত = 60 - 10 = 50 জন।
∴ নির্ণেয় fraction = 50/70
= 5/7

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ২৬) If the price of onion goes up by 25%, by how much should usage be reduced in order to keep the total expense for onion as before?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
পিয়াজের দাম বেড়ে 100 থেকে 125 হলো
∴ খরচ সমান রাখতে হলে, এখন 125 টাকায় কিনা যায় 1 অংশ
∴ 100 টাকায় কিনা যায় (1/125) × 100 অংশ
= 4/5 অংশ
∴ ব্যবহার কমাতে হবে = 1 - 4/5
= 1/5 অংশ।
অতএব, 1/5 × 100%
= 20% কমাতে হবে।

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ২৯) A football team has won 40 games out of 60 played. It has 32 more games to play. How many of these must the team win to make it a record 75% win for the season?
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
Team won 40 games out of 60 and the remaining games were 32.
Total games = 60 + 32
= 92
75% of 92 = 69
Team has to win 69 games in total.
Team has already won 40.
∴ Games to win = 69 - 40
= 29

Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.question: ৩০) A trader sells his goods at a discount of 20%. He still makes a profit of 25%. If he sells the goods at the marked price only, his profit will be:
Percentage, Profit & Loss, Discount.exp:
ধরি,
দ্রব্যটির বাজার মূল্য = 100 টাকা
∴ 20% ছাড়ে বিক্রয়মূল্য = (100 - 20) = 80 টাকা।
আবার, ধরি,
দ্রব্যটির উৎপাদন খরচ = x টাকা।
∴ x + x এর 25/100 = 80
⇒ x + x/4 = 80
⇒ 5x/4 = 80
⇒ x = 64

∴ Marked price (বাজার মূল্য) - এ পন্যটি বিক্রি করলে,
লাভ হয় - (100 - 64) = 36 টাকা।
∴ 64 টাকায় লাভ হয় = 36 টাকা
∴ 100 টাকায় লাভ হয় = (36 × 100)/64
                            = 56.25%
